Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows marked asymmetry with a smaller, hyperlucent right hemithorax and diminished vascular markings, which is characteristic of chronic obstruction or hypoplasia of the right pulmonary artery. This finding is consistent with Takayasu arteritis, a large-vessel vasculitis that frequently causes stenosis or occlusion of the pulmonary arteries, as confirmed by the calcified lesion in the right pulmonary artery on the accompanying CT scan.
